bsfa: Bayesian Stochastic Frontier Analysis

Source: R/bsfa-package.R
bsfa-package.Rd

Bayesian inference for stochastic frontier models by Markov chain Monte Carlo. Gibbs samplers with data augmentation are provided for composed-error frontier models in the tradition of van den Broeck, Koop, Osiewalski and Steel (1994), covering exponential and half-normal inefficiency, production and cost frontiers, and cross-sectional, time-invariant panel and four-component panel specifications. A model is built up step by step, by creating a model object and then adding priors, initial values and a seed to it before the posterior is drawn. Posterior distributions of unit-specific efficiency scores are obtained directly from the augmented draws rather than from point predictors.

References

Aigner, D., Lovell, C. A. K., & Schmidt, P. (1977). Formulation and estimation of stochastic frontier production function models. Journal of Econometrics, 6(1), 21–37.

Koop, G. (2003). Bayesian Econometrics. Chichester: Wiley.

Pitt, M. M., & Lee, L.-F. (1981). The measurement and sources of technical inefficiency in the Indonesian weaving industry. Journal of Development Economics, 9(1), 43–64.

Robert, C. P. (1995). Simulation of truncated normal variables. Statistics and Computing, 5(2), 121–125.

van den Broeck, J., Koop, G., Osiewalski, J., & Steel, M. F. J. (1994). Stochastic frontier models: A Bayesian perspective. Journal of Econometrics, 61(2), 273–303.
